newsitem.title: CHINA: China airline leases three Boeing 737 aircraft.
newsitem.headline: China airline leases three Boeing 737 aircraft.

text.p: A Chinese airline has signed an agreement to lease three Boing 737-300 planes for one year from 1997, officials said on Thursday.
China General Aviation Corporation (CGAC), an airline based in China's northern Shanxi province, signed the agreement on Monday to rent the three 148-seat Boeings, the Guangming Daily newspaper said.
The first aircraft would be handed over in May, 1997, with the remaining two following in June and July, it said.
The three airliners would ease CGAC's shortage of carrying capacity, said a company official contacted by telephone. She declined to give the name of the company that would provide the airliners.
While the original lease was only for one year, it could be extended depending on the airline's situation, she said but gave no details.
CGAC flew more than 50 domestic passenger and freight routes with more than 50 aircraft, another company official said.
The airline mainly relied on Soviet-made Yak-42s and Chinese Yun-7s, which had fewer seats than the Boeing 737s, he said.
